title: Exploring the Palmer Penguins Dataset with R

Loading the Data
First, I will load the dataset and display the first six rows.

library(palmerpenguins)

title: Exploring the Palmer Penguins Dataset with R
text:
Number of Penguins
I will count how many penguins belong to each species.

table(penguins$species)


   Adelie Chinstrap    Gentoo 
      152        68       124

title: Exploring the Palmer Penguins Dataset with R
text:
Comparing Species
Next, I will calculate the average body mass for each species.

average_mass <- aggregate(
  body_mass_g ~ species,
  data = penguins,
  FUN = mean
)

average_mass

    species body_mass_g
1    Adelie    3700.662
2 Chinstrap    3733.088
3    Gentoo    5076.016

title: Exploring the Palmer Penguins Dataset with R
text:
Visualization
I will create a bar chart to compare the average body mass of the three penguin species.

barplot(
  average_mass$body_mass_g,
  names.arg = average_mass$species,
  ylab = "Average Body Mass (g)",
  xlab = "Species"
)







Figure 1: Average body mass by penguin species.

title: Exploring the Palmer Penguins Dataset with R
text:
Conclusion
The results show that Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass among the three species. This analysis demonstrates how R can be used to summarize and visualize data.

title: Exploring the Palmer Penguins Dataset with Python
text:
Comparing Species
I will calculate the average body mass for each penguin species.

average_mass = penguins.groupby("species")["body_mass_g"].mean()
average_mass

title: Exploring the Palmer Penguins Dataset with Python
text:
Visualization
I will use a bar chart to compare the average body mass of each species.

average_mass.plot(kind="bar")
plt.ylabel("Average Body Mass (g)")
plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Average body mass by penguin species.

title: Exploring the Palmer Penguins Dataset with Python
text:
Conclusion
The chart shows that Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass among the three species. This simple analysis demonstrates how Python can be used to summarize and visualize data.
